generatedCommentsNodes.comment: Minor: this hunk only adds a trailing blank line before the closing brace of the class. It has no functional impact, but it is an unnecessary diff that adds noise to the change set.

The new `ReadOnlySlicedByteBuf` and `ReadOnlyDuplicatedByteBuf` inner classes (in `ReadOnlyByteBufferBuf`) extend the standard writable `SlicedByteBuf` / `DuplicatedByteBuf` and only override `isWritable()` / `isWritable(int)` to return `false`. However, they do **not** override the actual write methods (`setByte`, `writeByte`, `setInt`, `writeLong`, etc.) to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. In Netty's `AbstractByteBuf` hierarchy, write methods do not internally check `isWritable()` before mutating — they perform the write directly. This means a caller that invokes a write method without first checking `isWritable()` will silently succeed in mutating a buffer that is contractually "read-only."
The previous implementation (`new ReadOnlyByteBufferBuf(allocator, buffer)`) presumably inherited write-guarding from `ReadOnlyByteBufferBuf` itself. The new approach provides a weaker guarantee. Consider either:
- Extending a common read-only base that throws on all write operations, or
- Overriding the write methods in both inner classes to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`.

`testDuplicateSliceRelease` appears to contain a copy-paste error. The method name indicates a `duplicate()` followed by a `slice()`, but the body calls `buf.duplicate().duplicate()` — identical to `testDuplicateDuplicateRelease`. It should likely be:
```java
testRelease(buf, buf.duplicate().slice());
```
As written, the test does not actually exercise the `duplicate().slice()` path it claims to cover.

review_comment: The reason why read-only ByteBuffers are needed in the SslHandler use case is to avoid mutating the buffer. JDK's SSLEngine will mutate the input buffer with an in-place encryption reusing the input buffer unless the buffer is read-only. The support for read-only ByteBuffers in JDK's SSLEngine was added as a result of a bug reported by @chrisvest, more details in comment https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/14069#issuecomment-2129279047 .
